newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-ROFF HAT-TRICK SINKS NORTHERN TRANSVAAL.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-ROFF HAT-TRICK SINKS NORTHERN TRANSVAAL.

text.p: Wallaby winger Joe Roff scored a hat-trick of tries as Australian Capital Territory (ACT) moved into second place in the Super 12 table with a comprehensive 38-19 win over Northern Transvaal on Friday.
Roff transformed the match after half-time to reinforce the Brumbies' surprise challenge with their third victory in five games.

ACT, regarded as the weakest of Australia's three Super 12 representatives before the start of the season, earned four points for the win and an extra bonus point for scoring five tries at Bruce Stadium.
With 16 points from five games, the Brumbies are now two points behind leaders Gauteng Lions, formerly Transvaal, who have a game in hand.
"We certainly can't get carried away but we are reasonably happy with where we are," ACT coach Rod Macqueen said.
Third-placed Natal can lift themselves above ACT by beating struggling New South Wales at home on Saturday. Queensland, the third Australian team, prop up the Super 12 table.
Roff, who tormented the Northern Transvaal defence throughout, scored the first of his three tries immediately after the interval to stretch ACT's 8-5 halftime lead.

Winger Mitch Hardy scored in the corner within a minute to put the Brumbies in charge before Roff delighted the home crowd by running 60 metres to finish under the posts after collecting a chip ahead.
Roff had to wait until the final minute to complete his hat-trick, running on to another kick to outwit the demoralised Northern Transvaal defence.
Fly-half David Knox, who missed three of his four attempts at goal, found his touch eventually to finish with three penalties and two conversions.
Northern Transvaal replied with tries from centre Kosie Van Vuuren, hooker Jannie Brooks and winger Jacques Olivier. Theo Van Rensburg converted two of the tries.
The defeat leaves them struggling in mid-table with eight points from five games.
